List of file-system exercises. It doesn't explain why equal-sized disk reads vary in latency.
Covers concurrency and resource utilization. It mentions disk drives only as an example of a hardware resource and says nothing about why disk access times differ.

grades.quote: Because some disk accesses involve far more mechanical movement than others, the access time can vary substantially. In particular, contemporary disk drives can sustain data transfer rates measured in tens of megabytes per second if accessed optimally, but only tens of kilobytes per second if accessed randomly.
grades.reason: Says access time varies because some accesses need far more mechanical movement than others. It gives the sequential-versus-random throughput gap and describes the platters, spinning, and pivoting head arm. It never names seek time or rotational latency, so it is useful but only partly complete.
